messages:
jules: Heads-up: after last night's kernel+batching merge we're observing a measurable host-side overhead on short streaming requests. pprof shows repeated selector scoring and extra kv churn.
priya: when did the merge land and which regions?
jules: merged 2026-03-25T22:40 UTC, rolled to canary (15%). spikes in us-central and eu-west. sample top functions from a 20s CPU profile below.
ci-bot: deploy 2026-03-25T22:38 by @ci-bot (selector-batcher:20260325) -> canary 15% -> promoted 22:39
matt: paste the top functions please.
jules: sanitized pprof top:
```
# top 10
17.1% kernel_selector::score_candidates
13.4% kv_cache::lookup
10.8% http2::hpack_decode
8.9% parse::proto_frame
7.2% tokenize::scan_utf8
6.5% batch_coordinator::emit_chunk
5.0% writev::flush
3.0% sched::sleep
2.1% telemetry::send
```
yvonne: kernel_selector scoring that high is odd. the change was supposed to move more work to the sidecar, not increase host scoring. Could selector be rescoring per chunk?
priya: yes, batching change reschedules scoring when the batch window shrinks. that means for fragmented streaming requests we call score_candidates O(chunks) instead of once per request.
jules: kv miss-rate jumped ~15% and variant_id churn looks correlated with selector outputs. keys include a variant_stamp field now. ops-bot: we see evictions up and more lock contention on kv store.
matt: reproduction plan: run vegeta with streaming pattern or wrk lua to mimic multiplexed small prompts. example wrk: `wrk -t6 -c200 -d45s --latency 'lua_stream_short.lua' http://ingress:8080/v1/stream` where lua emits 30-70 token messages and reads frames. capture `go tool pprof -http=:8081 /tmp/ingress.cpu` during run.
priya: quick mitigations: 1) revert rescore-on-shrink behavior to previous semantics on canary 2) add selector memoization keyed by (route, model, quant_profile, small_input=true) 3) stabilize variant_id generation to exclude ephemeral stamps 4) add metrics: selector_calls_per_request, kv_evictions_per_min, hpack_decodes_per_request, batch_efficiency_ratio.
jules: i'm starting a canary rollback now for selector-batcher. if CPU drops we know the change pathway is culprit.
ci-bot: rollback initiated at 22:50 by @jules -> canary 15% -> in progress
yvonne: long-term fixes: ensure selector is called at most once per logical request unless batch-level features change; if we must rescore, do it at batch boundaries, not chunk boundaries. also ensure memo cache has LRU TTL and is invalidated on model/route changes.
matt: also audit tokenization fastpaths; minor branching changes there magnify when selector calls increase. add regression tests for 0-128 token path and hpack-fragmented frames.
priya: follow-ups assigned: - jules: rollback + postmortem draft - matt: wrk/vegeta reproduction + pprofs (before/after) - yvonne: variant_id audit + KV key stability patch - ops-bot: add the new telemetry metrics to dashboards
jules: thanks all. posting flamegraphs and pprof links once tests complete. will keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
